I have zero faith that they can pull this off successfully. From an investor standpoint, reddit has been dead for several years. They only have two real choices:

The first was to become a chan-style board, rough around the edges with NSFW content. They would need to tolerate raids, insults, porn, gore, and general misbehavior. Admins would only need to take down illegal content and comply with takedown requests. The benefit is that this model is cheap and easy. However, it wouldn't make big bucks, just perhaps enough to cover hosting. No big advertisers, so no perks, stock options, or status.

The second is to go full-SFW, which would require paid employee mods and rigid content guidelines. CoonTown would only be the beginning; they would have to ban all porn, gore, drama, "hate," and so on. Language and disobedience would also have to be policed. This reddit would perhaps resemble 新浪微博, the chatrooms on Wii, or the comments sections on NYT. Obviously, the users would revolt. This kills reddit, for all intents and purposes. A shell would be left, and they'd have to bank that it is enough to sustain the site.

The investors are morons for ever putting a dollar into that site. If I was one, I'd sell, but if I couldn't, I'd have demanded the SFW conversion years ago. It's a Hail Mary to save the value of the enterprise, and it is almost certain to fail. However, it is their only real option.

The last option is, like the zombie banks, to remain zombie reddit. They chug along on wishful thinking and cheap credit until one day the lights go out. Honestly, I can see this as the most likely possibility. Reddit right now is both unprofitable and in a Catch 22, and the temptation is just to muddle forward until ruined by exogenous forces.
